content:
Apple today unveiled two new Apple Silicon chips. The M6 chip debuts in a new Mac mini model, marking Apple's first 2-nanometer processor. The M5 Ultra, meanwhile, appears in an upgraded Mac Studio and is the most powerful chip Apple has ever created.

Apple's All-New M6 Chip

The M6 is Apple's first 2-nanometer chip. Apple says it delivers improved transistor density and power efficiency, allowing the company to scale up its compute blocks without increasing the chip's size.

The M6 features a 12-core CPU, two more cores than the M5. Notably, this is Apple's first processor to combine three types of CPU cores simultaneously: two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores.

Super cores prioritize extreme single-thread performance and are Apple's most powerful core type; performance cores are optimized for demanding multi-threaded workloads; efficiency cores handle background operations.

Apple says this gives the M6 "the world's fastest single-thread performance" and delivers "up to 1.2x faster multi-threaded performance than the M5."

The M6 comes with a 12-core GPU, two more cores than the M5, with each core featuring a Neural Accelerator. Apple says this delivers a 30% increase in peak GPU compute for AI compared to the M5. The M6 GPU also features an updated shader core architecture, Dynamic Caching, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing.

The M6 supports up to 32GB of unified memory, with memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s—up to 10% faster than the M5.

In addition, the M6 can process the FP8 format directly in hardware, whereas the M5 required software-based FP8 handling. FP8 is an 8-bit format designed to make AI workloads faster and more memory-efficient.

M6 Specifications and Benchmarks:

  • CPU: Multi-threaded performance up to 1.2x faster than M5, and 2.4x faster than M1.
  • GPU AI Compute: Peak AI GPU compute nearly 30% higher than M5, and over 8x higher than M1.
  • Geometry Performance: 50% faster geometry throughput for complex image processing.
  • Neural Engine: Dual 16-core Neural Engines deliver up to 2x higher peak compute performance than the previous generation.
  • Memory Bandwidth: Up to 170GB/s, 10% higher than M5, and 2.5x that of M1.

The M6 launches today alongside the new Mac mini—see our full coverage for details.

M5 Ultra

At the high end, Apple unveiled the M5 Ultra, which the company calls "the most powerful chip we've ever built." The biggest change is that the M5 Ultra uses a new-generation UltraFusion technology.

Apple explains that the new-generation UltraFusion technology connects two dual-chiplet M5 Max configurations, creating Apple's first four-chiplet architecture. The new UltraFusion design provides over 4.4TB/s of chip-to-chip interconnect bandwidth and more than 6x the connection density of before, allowing all four chips to operate as a single unified processor.

The M5 Ultra offers up to a 36-core CPU, comprising 12 super cores and 24 performance cores. Apple says this delivers up to 1.25x the single-thread performance and 1.3x the multi-threaded performance of the M3 Ultra.

On the graphics side, the M5 Ultra features a new-generation GPU with up to 80 cores, each equipped with a Neural Accelerator. Apple says the M5 Ultra delivers up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute performance for AI compared to the M3 Ultra.

Additional M5 Ultra GPU specifications include:

  • Apple's latest shader cores with second-generation Dynamic Caching
  • Hardware-accelerated mesh shading
  • Third-generation ray tracing

Overall, Apple says the M5 Ultra delivers up to 40% faster graphics performance than the M3 Ultra.

The M5 Ultra supports up to 512GB of unified memory, with memory bandwidth of up to 1.2TB/s—50% higher than the M3 Ultra.

M5 Ultra Specifications and Benchmarks

  • CPU: Up to 1.25x faster single-thread performance and 1.3x faster multi-threaded performance than M3 Ultra.
  • GPU AI Compute: Peak AI GPU compute is 4.5x that of the M3 Ultra, and over 6x that of the M1 Ultra.
  • Graphics Performance: Up to 40% faster than M3 Ultra.
  • Memory Bandwidth: 1.2TB/s, 50% higher than M3 Ultra.

The M5 Ultra launches today alongside the new Mac Studio—see our full coverage for details.
